sections.body: Food labels show what's inside: energy (calories), fat, sugar, salt and more, usually per 100 g and per portion.
Ingredients are listed from MOST to LEAST. If sugar is first, there's more sugar than anything else!
Some countries use traffic-light colours: green = low, amber = medium, red = high.
The WHO recommends keeping 'free sugars' (added sugars, plus honey and fruit juice) to less than 10% of daily energy.

quiz.q: Ingredients are listed in what order?
hints: The first ingredient is the biggest part.
The list goes from biggest amount to smallest.
If flour is first in a bread label, there's more flour than anything else. What does that tell you about the order?
quiz.explain: Ingredients go from most to least by weight.

quiz.q: Cereal A: 30 g sugar per 100 g. Cereal B: 5 g per 100 g. Which has less sugar?
hints: Drink X has 10 g sugar per 100 ml; drink Y has 2 g. Y has less.
quiz.explain: Cereal B has much less sugar (5 g vs 30 g per 100 g).

quiz.q: On a traffic-light food label, what does red mean?
hints: Think about what a red traffic light tells drivers to do.
Green means low and amber means medium.
Example: a label shows green for fat. That means the food is low in fat.
quiz.explain: On these labels, red means high, amber means medium and green means low.
